whatToWatch.text: Seattle's defense is the real deal — just 17.9 points allowed per game and 2.43 sacks a night. At 4-3 with a win streak going and a field-goal line in their favor at home, this is the kind of game good teams bank.

Pass rush vs. pass rush: the Bears are actually getting home slightly more often (2.71 sacks per game to Seattle's 2.43), but they're also giving up 20.4 points a game. Somebody's quarterback is going to have a long afternoon — the 46.5 total says the books think points will be hard to come by.

Injury edge tilts Seattle's way: nobody's ruled out for the Hawks, though five guys carry a questionable tag including Chazz Surratt, Drake Thomas and Drew Lock. Chicago's down two in Anthony Johnson Jr. and Jack Sanborn — watch whether Seattle attacks those spots early.

newsBlurb.text: Lumen Field hosts the Bears on Monday night, and the Week 8 spotlight belongs entirely to Seattle. Chicago walks into the loudest building in the league with no Sunday crowd noise to hide behind — a standalone national window, one game, full volume.
